official_sources: Planning and Infrastructure Act commencement regulations

official_measurement_examples.name: Current 1 April 2026 fees
official_measurement_examples.fact: The March-July 2026 consultation records the fees applicable from 1 April 2026 separately from the proposed National Default Fee schedule; proposed figures must not be treated as already operative fees.

official_measurement_examples.name: Government response timing
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 16 July 2026 government response says national fee increases are intended through regulations before year-end, subject to Parliamentary approval; this is not evidence that the proposed schedule was already in force on 26 July 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: Local fee-setting power
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Planning and Infrastructure Act 2025 creates powers for regulations to authorise or require local fee setting, but the existence of the power is not itself proof that a particular authority has an operative locally varied fee today.

official_measurement_examples.name: Statutory-consultee surcharge
official_measurement_examples.fact: The July 2026 response says the surcharge requires further design and consultation; an indicative percentage is not an operative charge on a specific application.

official_measurement_examples.name: Application-type separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Householder, full, outline, prior-approval, section 73, discharge-of-condition, PiP and other fee categories use different fee structures and must not be silently interchanged.

official_measurement_examples.name: NSIP fee separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Inspectorate NSIP charges are a separate Planning Act 2008 fee regime and must not be applied as Town and Country Planning Act local application fees.

official_measurement_examples.name: Fee payment not permission
official_measurement_examples.fact: Payment of the correct planning fee validates the financial component of an application process; it does not grant planning permission or prove policy compliance.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A national or local application fee does not determine land ownership, planning outcome, viability or final development yield.

core_rules: current fee is not proposed future fee
government response is not enacted fee regulation
local fee-setting power is not proof of local implementation
indicative surcharge is not operative surcharge
1 April 2026 current fee date must be retained
NSIP charges are separate from TCPA application fees
fee payment is not planning permission
fee payment is not validation of all documents
fee does not calculate development yield
consultation proposal must retain proposal status
no parcel fee-based clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official MHCLG/GOV.UK and legislation.gov.uk sources checked 2026-07-26. The 16 July 2026 government response was retained with clear separation between fees applicable from 1 April 2026, proposed National Default Fees, future local fee setting and a future statutory-consultee surcharge; no parcel promotion.
